classification: Authored junior-astronaut learning campaign. Hardware capacities, power budgets, failures and shelter alerts are fictional teaching scenarios. Elevation, coordinates, slopes and dated celestial vectors retain NASA/JPL provenance.

levels.title: Your first moonwalk
levels.brief: Learn to move, identify yourself and your destination, record a real terrain observation, and return to Haven.
steps: Walk 40 m toward the cyan training beacon
Press Q at the beacon to measure the terrain
Return to Haven and press E
levels.question: What makes the white Lifeline route useful before a detour?
answers: It estimates whether my current supplies support a return
It makes the suit's oxygen unlimited
It marks the fastest path to every planet
levels.explanation: The Lifeline calculates a terrain route and compares its oxygen, water and energy cost with your remaining supplies. A longer detour changes that calculation.

levels.title: Keep Haven alive
levels.brief: Restore the outpost power bus, then allocate available power to life support, food production and communications. Every system has a minimum demand.
steps: Press E at Haven and reconnect its power circuit
Allocate power to cover all three system demands
Leave a reserve within the available supply
levels.question: What happens if total allocated power exceeds the supply?
answers: All systems automatically receive extra energy
The allocation cannot be supported; reduce or reprioritise loads
Only the displayed numbers change
levels.explanation: The outpost has a finite power supply. Allocations above that limit are rejected. Meeting life-support demand and leaving a reserve keeps the teaching model stable.

levels.title: Bring Echo home
levels.brief: Use your field skills on a full recovery expedition. Restore the relay, repair Echo, board it and drive it home while protecting your return reserves.
steps: Reach the relay and repair its circuit
Reach Echo and repair its power bus
Board Echo, drive to Haven and press E to dock
levels.question: Why can a walking shortcut be unavailable to Echo?
answers: Rover routes ignore terrain elevations
The rover uses a stricter slope limit than the suit
The Sun blocks every rover path
levels.explanation: Both paths are derived from the NASA elevation grid. The fictional rover is configured for a lower maximum slope, so its route can differ from an EVA route.

levels.title: Read the Moon and sky
levels.brief: Visit two survey sites, inspect Earth and LRO in the orbital tracker, and bring your findings back. Learn the difference between your surface position and dated spacecraft positions.
steps: Scan the two marked survey sites with Q
Inspect Earth and LRO in the orbital tracker
Return to Haven and press E
levels.question: Are the orbital positions live signals from the spacecraft?
answers: Yes, they are live telemetry from the suit
No, they are interpolated dated JPL ephemerides
They are random positions drawn for each game
levels.explanation: The orbital tracker uses cached NASA/JPL samples at the mission clock. The surface tracker reads your character's game state in a separate lunar body-fixed frame.

levels.title: Protect the crew
levels.brief: Complete a clearly labelled training alert: return from the field, enter Haven, seal the shelter and keep essential systems powered under a reduced supply. No real radiation dose is modelled.
steps: Return from the field to Haven
Press E to operate the shelter systems
Seal the shelter and balance emergency power
levels.question: What is the sensible response to this shelter training alert?
answers: Stay outside and keep collecting optional observations
Return to shelter and prioritise life support within the power budget
Turn every system to its maximum allocation
levels.explanation: The drill rewards reaching shelter, sealing it and supplying essential loads within a finite budget. It teaches decision priorities; it is an authored scenario, not a lunar radiation forecast.

levels.title: Harvest the sunlight
levels.brief: Visit the outpost array, use its live 3D controls to aim both axes, and commission a useful power source.
steps: Inspect the array at Haven
Align tilt and bearing with the training target
Connect the array when its alignment is correct
levels.question: Why does the modeled output change as the array turns?
answers: Orientation affects the teaching model's collected power
Every angle always produces maximum power
The panel creates energy without a source
levels.explanation: The visible array orientation feeds the modeled power calculation. The angles and light direction are authored teaching targets, not observed lunar illumination.

levels.title: Prepare for an EVA
levels.brief: Operate a visible airlock: check your suit, seal the inner hatch, vent the chamber, then open the outer hatch. Incorrect action order is rejected.
steps: Check suit reserves at the airlock
Seal the inner hatch and vent the chamber
Open the outer hatch after pressure is reduced
levels.question: What must happen before opening the outer hatch?
answers: Open both hatches together
Seal the inner hatch and depressurise the chamber
Ignore the suit check
levels.explanation: The procedure isolates the outpost before venting the teaching-model chamber. Hatch motion and pressure indicators show the sequence; this is not a certified EVA procedure.

levels.title: Bring back a lunar sample
levels.brief: Walk to the marked sample, collect it, bring it to Haven, attach its measured site record, seal the canister and stow it in the laboratory.
steps: Reach the field sample and press E to collect it
Return the sample to the laboratory at Haven
Attach its site record, seal it and stow it
levels.question: Why keep a site record with the sample?
answers: It preserves where the observation was collected
It increases oxygen without a refill
It makes every lunar rock identical
levels.explanation: The specimen is fictional, but its collection coordinates and elevation come from the NASA terrain grid. Its label keeps that observation attached to the stored sample.

levels.title: Restore the ground link
levels.brief: Travel to the relay and aim its physical dish at an authored training beacon. Inspect it from any side while adjusting bearing and elevation.
steps: Reach the relay station
Align the dish bearing and elevation
Establish the training link
levels.question: What are the antenna controls changing?
answers: The real orbit of the Moon
The physical dish orientation and modeled alignment quality
The total number of NASA satellites
levels.explanation: The 3D dish follows your inputs and the game evaluates alignment against a fictional ground-beacon target. It does not calculate a real lunar radio link.

levels.title: Complete the supply run
levels.brief: Secure a visible supply crate onto Echo, board it, deliver the crate to the field station, then return to Haven. Complete this practical run to graduate.
steps: Load the supply crate at Haven and board Echo
Drive to the field station and press E to unload
Return Echo to Haven and press E to dock
levels.question: What makes a supply run complete?
answers: Driving away without a loaded crate
Delivering the cargo and bringing the rover safely home
Leaving the rover at an unmarked point
levels.explanation: The task records loading, transport, delivery and docking as separate actions. The actual 3D crate changes position as it moves from the outpost to the rover and field station.
